thesis: A beta carried the week's real work in secrets, backups, and setup, while stable held steady and upgrade paths still need care.

slides.label: Week 21
slides.title: OpenClaw Change log & Dev Experience
slides.lead: Beta shipped, stable held, and commit activity stayed high across the OpenClaw project.

cards.title: This week at a glance
items: v2026.8.1-beta.2 published Aug 15
No stable release inside the window
2,193 commits from 89 authors
Secrets, backups, and local setup all moved

slides.label: Release window
slides.title: No stable release this week
slides.lead: The only release inside the window was a beta. Stable and extended-stable both sit outside the window, unchanged.

cards.title: Release ledger

Stable: openclaw@2026.7.1-2, published Aug 4, outside the window

No stable release published Aug 14 through 21

slides.label: Theme
slides.title: Secrets and plugin provenance
slides.lead: Beta work tightened where secrets can travel and who gets to run unverified code.

cards.title: Secret egress host binding
items: Ties shared-store secrets to exact HTTPS destination hosts
Fails closed before any plaintext egress

cards.title: Plugin trust
items: Arbitrary executable plugin sources now require explicit --force
Trusted ClawHub, bundled, official, and tracked update flows stay low-friction

slides.label: Theme
slides.title: Backup and recovery
slides.lead: New snapshot commands and isolated app profiles give operators a real recovery path.

cards.title: SQLite snapshots
items: openclaw backup sqlite create, list, verify, restore
Verified global and per-agent artifacts
Restore only targets fresh targets

cards.title: macOS app profiles
items: Named profiles isolate state and preferences
Keychain and Gateway services isolated per profile
Duplicate-instance ownership handled per profile

slides.label: Theme
slides.title: Runtime and model switching
slides.lead: Model switching got a new engine, and local setup got more paths to a working model.

cards.title: GPT-5.6 Ultra support
items: Adds Sol, Terra, and Luna across OpenClaw and Codex engines
Atomic runtime, model, and thinking switching through /model
Fallback included

cards.title: Local model setup
items: Surfaces Ollama, llama.cpp, and LM Studio
Retries unavailable LM Studio services
Verifies the exact prepared model

cards.title: First-run setup
items: Verified model setup now continues into Custodian
Channels are optional during first run

slides.label: Theme
slides.title: Channel ingress, Control UI, CDP
slides.lead: Ingress monitors, Control UI recovery, and a new CDP path for the browser extension.

cards.title: Channel-plugin ingress
items: Shared monitors add durable admission, polling, pruning
Claim identity validation and adoption handoff
Shutdown lifecycle included

cards.title: Control UI recovery
items: Update recovery waits through gateway restart
Reloads once the gateway responds

cards.title: Browser extension relay
items: Answers Target.getBrowserContexts
Serves a DevTools-style /json/list
Adds openclaw browser extension cdp for external clients

slides.label: Theme
slides.title: External supervision and MCP dashboards
slides.lead: External lifecycle owners get a real boundary, and dashboard widgets get lease-based grants.

cards.title: External supervision
items: OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external
Blocks native service mutation under external ownership
Blocks self-update under external ownership

cards.title: MCP dashboards
items: Dashboard MCP Apps can be pinned as living widgets
Lease renewal keeps pinned widgets alive
Grants are revision-bound

slides.label: Developer experience
slides.title: DX review
slides.lead: The release notes are direct about what passed and what didn't ahead of promotion.

cards.title: What passed
items: Packaged Telegram, Docker assets, clean install and update
Plugin runtime checks and targeted Docker lanes
An isolated live model turn

cards.title: What did not
items: Full Release Validation did not pass
An unbound context-engine session could fall back to the default agent
Release tooling and test fixtures also failed

cards.title: Guidance from the release
items: Don't promote this beta to stable without a fixed successor
Don't promote without green full validation

slides.label: Developer experience
slides.title: Community signal
slides.accent: Answer Overflow, public historical Discord search
slides.lead: Upgrade recovery is where most of the reported friction sits, from plugin versions to service state.

cards.title: Upgrade friction
items: Four official plugins stayed on 2026.7.2-beta.7 after updating to 2026.8.1-beta.1
Gateway startup failed until plugins and service state were repaired
A gateway service from 2026.7.2-beta.7 remained after the CLI moved on, causing a service/config mismatch

cards.title: Install gaps
items: An exact beta plugin install hit npm ETARGET, @openclaw/codex@2026.8.1-beta.1 was not published
A cron blocking report surfaced on 2026.8.1-beta.2, version marker only, no confirmed root cause

cards.title: Where things stood
items: Community support confirmed stable stayed openclaw@2026.7.1-2 as of Aug 19
Beta was 2026.8.1-beta.2 at that same check

slides.label: Developer experience
slides.title: Signal map
slides.lead: Stronger primitives landed, but they arrive on a beta whose own validation hasn't gone green.

cards.title: What's landing
items: Backup primitives: SQLite snapshot commands
Setup primitives: local model detection, first-run flow
Trust primitives: secret egress binding, plugin --force gating

cards.title: What needs attention
items: Upgrade recovery concentrates around core, plugin, and service version alignment
Full Release Validation was not green for beta.2

cards.title: Before upgrading
items: Check plugin versions match the target release
Check gateway service state after any CLI upgrade

slides.label: Weekly close
slides.title: Where OpenClaw stands
slides.lead: v2026.8.1-beta.2 holds the week's real progress in secrets, backups, and setup. Stable is still openclaw@2026.7.1-2, and that beta needs a fixed successor with green full validation before it moves to stable.

cards.title: Concrete takeaway
items: Run beta.2 for the new backup and setup tools if you can tolerate beta risk
Keep stable at openclaw@2026.7.1-2 for anything that can't
